title: Fitting ideals of a finite module: independence of generators and base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and let $k\ge0$ be an integer. For an $R$-linear surjection $\pi:R^{\oplus n}\to M$ with kernel $K\subset R^{\oplus n}$, let $I_k(\pi)\subset R$ be the ideal generated by the $(n-k)\times(n-k)$ minors of all $(n-k)\times n$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] whose rows are elements of $K$, with $I_k(\pi)=R$ when $n\le k$. Then: (1) $I_k(\pi)=I_k(\pi')$ for any two $R$-linear surjections $\pi:R^{\oplus n}\to M$ and $\pi':R^{\oplus n'}\to M$; (2) for every ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$, the surjection $\pi\otimes_RR':R'^{\oplus n}\to M\otimes_RR'$ satisfies $I_k(\pi\otimes_RR')=\varphi(I_k(\pi))R'$. In particular, for $g\in R$ the ideal $I_k$ of the $R_g$-module $M_g$ is $I_k(\pi)R_g$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal) for (1), including the description by minors of matrices with rows in the kernel given at the start of its proof; Lemma Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics) part (3) for (2); used in Divisors Section Tag 0C3C (section-fitting-ideals) to glue the Fitting ideal sheaves

proof.text: Fix $k\ge0$. For any finite matrix $A$, use $J_r(A)$ as in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-minor-inclusions]. If $n>k$ and $r=n-k$, then $I_k(\pi)$ is generated by $J_r(A)$ as $A$ ranges over all finite matrices with $n$ columns and rows in $K=\ker\pi$: every $r$-minor uses just $r$ rows, and these are exactly the rows allowed in the defining row-minor description of $I_k(\pi)$. No finite generation of $K$ is needed.

source.place: 07Z8, opening kernel-row description, allowing finite lists of arbitrary length

proof.text: Adjoin $d\ge0$ zero generators, so $\pi^+=(\pi,0):R^{\oplus(n+d)}\to M$ has kernel $K\oplus R^{\oplus d}$. First suppose $n>k$ and put $r=n-k>0$. Pad any $r$ kernel rows by zeros and append the last $d$ standard basis vectors. The minor selecting their $r$ old columns and all $d$ new columns is block diagonal with blocks the original minor and $1_d$; the Leibniz formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] makes its determinant the original determinant. Hence $I_k(\pi)\subseteq I_k(\pi^+)$.

source.place: 07Z8, stabilization paragraph, first inclusion; block determinant expanded from its definition

proof.text: Conversely, still with $n>k$, take any $(r+d)$ rows in $K\oplus R^{\oplus d}$, forming a matrix $B$ with $n+d$ columns, and let $A$ be its first $n$ columns. Its rows lie in $K$. Clause (2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-minor-inclusions] gives $J_{r+d}(B)\subseteq J_r(A)\subseteq I_k(\pi)$, proving the reverse inclusion. If $n\le k$, then $I_k(\pi)=R$. When $n+d\le k$ the stabilized ideal is also $R$ by convention; otherwise $0<t=n+d-k\le d$, and $t$ of the added basis vectors give a $t$-minor equal to $1$. Thus $I_k(\pi^+)=I_k(\pi)$ in every case.

source.place: 07Z8, stabilization paragraph, reverse inclusion via 07Z7 and the unit-ideal boundary cases

proof.text: An automorphism $u$ of $R^{\oplus N}$ replaces each row $z$ by $zC$ for an invertible $N\times N$ matrix $C$. For $N>k$, clause (3) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-minor-inclusions] puts every $(N-k)$-minor of $AC$ in $J_{N-k}(A)$, so the ideal for $u(K)$ is contained in the ideal for $K$. Applying the same statement to $C^{-1}$ reverses the inclusion. For $N\le k$ both ideals are $R$ by convention. Therefore isomorphic free presentations of the same rank have equal ideals.

source.place: 07Z8, final paragraph: invariance under an invertible change of free coordinates, using 07Z7(3)

proof.text:
Compare $\pi:F=R^{\oplus n}\to M$ and $\pi':G=R^{\oplus m}\to M$. Lift the images of the finitely many standard basis vectors, using the two surjections, to obtain linear maps $f:G\to F$ and $g:F\to G$ with $\pi f=\pi'$ and $\pi'g=\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The map
$$U:F\oplus G\longrightarrow G\oplus F,\quad U(x,y)=(y+g(x-fy),x-fy)$$
has inverse $U^{-1}(u,v)=(v+f(u-gv),u-gv)$, by substitution, and $(\pi',0)U(x,y)=\pi'(y)+\pi(x-fy)=\pi(x)$. Thus $U$ identifies the kernels of the two zero-stabilized presentations, both of rank $n+m$. Apply Step 4 and then the stabilization equalities in Steps 2-3 to obtain $I_k(\pi)=I_k(\pi')$. This explicit shear calculation supplies the commuting presentation isomorphism used at the Schanuel step of 07Z8; it uses no claim about an abstract isomorphism of kernels lifting automatically.

source.place: 07Z8, final paragraph, commuting stabilized-presentation comparison written explicitly by two invertible shears

proof.text: For a ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] with $M_1=K$, $M_2=R^{\oplus n}$, $M_3=M$, $N=R'$ to $K\hookrightarrow R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\pi}M\to0$. It gives surjectivity of $\pi\otimes1$ and identifies its kernel $K'$ with the image of $K\otimes_RR'$, without asserting this tensor map is injective. The tensor construction [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $R^{\oplus n}\otimes_RR'$ with $R'^{\oplus n}$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto(a\varphi(x_j))_j$; its inverse sends $(a_j)_j$ to $\sum_j e_j\otimes a_j$. Since pure tensors generate, each row of $K'$ is a finite $R'$-linear combination of images of rows of $K$.

source.place: 07ZA, proof of (3), right exactness of tensor and the base-changed presentation

proof.text:
If $n\le k$, both base-change ideals are the unit ideal. Otherwise put $r=n-k>0$. Fix $r$ rows in $K'$ and a set of $r$ columns. Write each row as a finite sum $z'_i=\sum_\alpha a_{i\alpha}\varphi(z_{i\alpha})$, with $z_{i\alpha}\in K$, as supplied by Step 6. Substituting these finite sums in the Leibniz formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] and distributing products gives
$$\det(z'_i|_J)_i=\sum_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r}\Bigl(\prod_i a_{i\alpha_i}\Bigr)\varphi\bigl(\det(z_{i\alpha_i}|_J)_i\bigr).$$
Every summand lies in $\varphi(I_k(\pi))R'$. Conversely the image of each original minor is the minor on the image rows, which lie in $K'$. Taking the generated ideals proves $I_k(\pi\otimes_RR')=\varphi(I_k(\pi))R'$. This is a direct finite-sum calculation, with no flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: 07ZA(3), determinant calculation after tensoring the presentation; expanded from the Leibniz formula

proof.text: Finally take $R'=R_g$. The natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] sends $m\otimes(a/g^e)$ to $am/g^e$ and carries $\pi\otimes1$ to $\pi_g$. Thus Step 7 computes the ideal of this presentation of $M_g$ as $I_k(\pi)R_g$; presentation independence from Step 5 makes it the ideal of $M_g$ itself.

source.place: 07ZA(3), specialization to the ring localization R to R_g

lean.statement: theorem presentationFittingIdeal_independence_baseChange {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℕ) {n : ℕ} (π : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (hπ : Function.Surjective π) : (∀ (n' : ℕ) (π' : (Fin n' → R) →ₗ[R] M), Function.Surjective π' → π.presentationFittingIdeal k = π'.presentationFittingIdeal k) ∧ (∀ (A : Type w) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A], Function.Surjective (π.baseChangePresentation A) ∧ (π.baseChangePresentation A).presentationFittingIdeal k = Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) (π.presentationFittingIdeal k)) ∧ (∀ g : R, Function.Surjective (π.localizePresentationAway g) ∧ (π.localizePresentationAway g).presentationFittingIdeal k = Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away g)) (π.presentationFittingIdeal k))
